[element-std-org]
=== `<std-org>` Standards Organization Description

A container element to hold the organization name, abbreviated name, and location information for one of the standards organizations responsible for publishing or adopting the standard.

#### Usage/Remarks
The <<element-std-org,`<std-org>`>> element provides a descriptive name and location information about the publisher/adopter of a standards document, in the same way that the element `<publisher>` in JATS provides name and location information concerning the publisher of a journal article.
#### One Organization Per Element

There may be several standards organizations responsible for a standards document, and each will be named in a separate <<element-std-org,`<std-org>`>> element.
#### Part Played

The <<attribute-std-org-role,`@std-org-role`>> attribute can be used to record what part the standards organization played in the standard, such as “`lead`”, “`co-producer`”, etc.

#### Related Elements

Several elements inside the container element <<element-std-org,`<std-org>`>> provide the name and location of a publishing or adopting standards organization: <<element-std-org-name,`<std-org-name>`>> provides an official, typically longer, name of an organization (“International Business Machinery”). <<element-std-org-abbrev,`<std-org-abbrev>`>> provides a short name or acronym for the organization (“IBM”). <<element-std-org-loc,`<std-org-loc>`>> names one or more locations where the organization operates, which may be as small as a city name or may include a complete address.
*SDO, Originator, and SDO-Organization:* The element <<element-std-org-abbrev,`<std-org-abbrev>`>> inside <<element-std-org,`<std-org>`>> can replace both the <<element-originator,`<originator>`>> element and the <<element-sdo,`<sdo>`>> element used in earlier ISO STS processing.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-std-org-level,`@std-org-level`>>
* <<attribute-std-org-role,`@std-org-role`>>
* <<attribute-std-org-type,`@std-org-type`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-iso-meta,`<iso-meta>`>>, <<element-nat-meta,`<nat-meta>`>>, <<element-reg-meta,`<reg-meta>`>>, <<element-std-doc-meta,`<std-doc-meta>`>>, <<element-std-meta,`<std-meta>`>>, <<element-std-org-group,`<std-org-group>`>>
#### Description

The following, in order: <<element-std-org-name,`<std-org-name>`>> <<element-std-org-name,Standards Organization Name>>, zero or one <<element-std-org-abbrev,`<std-org-abbrev>`>> <<element-std-org-abbrev,Standards Organization Abbreviated Name>>, zero or more <<element-std-org-loc,`<std-org-loc>`>> <<element-std-org-loc,Standards Organization Location>>, zero or more
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  std-org      %std-org-model;                              >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(std-org-name?, std-org-abbrev*, std-org-loc*)

#### Tagged Sample

##### Typical `<std-org>` with name, abbreviation, and location
[source,xml]
....
...
<std-org-group>
 <std-org std-org-type="sdo" std-org-role="co-producer" std-org-level="1">
  <std-org-name>American Society of Mechanical Engineers</std-org-name>
  <std-org-abbrev>ASME</std-org-abbrev>
  <std-org-loc
   ><addr-line>2 Park Ave.</addr-line>
   <city>New York</city>
   <state>NY</state>
   <postal-code>10016</postal-code>
   <uri>https://www.asme.org/</uri></std-org-loc>
 </std-org>

 <std-org std-org-type="sdo" std-org-role="co-producer" std-org-level="2">
  <std-org-name>American Petroleum Institute</std-org-name>
  <std-org-abbrev>API</std-org-abbrev>
  <std-org-loc
   ><addr-line>1220 L Street, N.W.</addr-line>
   <city>Washington</city>
   <state>D.C.</state>
   <postal-code>20005</postal-code>
   <uri>http://www.api.org/</uri></std-org-loc>
 </std-org>
</std-org-group>
...
....
